opportunities.title: Coverage-stratified sampling over rotation and feature cells
opportunities.question: Does steering generation toward under-evaluated rotation-subfamily x feature cells find qualifying signals that uniform random_weighted sampling misses at the same completed-evaluation count?
opportunities.mechanism: Maintain a construction-time coverage ledger over enumerable cells. The runnable policy (examples/agent-campaign/stratified_policy.py) stratifies over the documented generator callables (random_weighted, genetic) with measured-depth descriptors; the offline fixture stratifies over rotation x feature cells. Target the least-covered cell with bounded duplicate attempts, count duplicates and depth rejections separately from completed evaluations, and checkpoint the policy RNG and history. Per-candidate leaf attribution is not a public API; when it cannot be observed, record feature_attribution as unavailable with a reason rather than the full catalogue or fabricated cells.
opportunities.primary_source_note: MAP-Elites. A starting point for quality-diversity archives, not evidence of superiority over random_weighted.
opportunities.baseline_comparison: Matched baseline (installed genetic by default; random_weighted as the documented alternative, with no full GA benchmark claimed) and the stratified template on the same era/config, seed set, and equal completed evaluator counts, isolated per signal_pool_name; compare get_search_stats rows grouped by function subfamily x feature subfamily and get_yield_analysis lifetime_yield_rate. Per-era segments only; no pooling across era boundaries.
opportunities.acceptance_evidence: Preregistered hypothesis and direction; paired independent runs with matched budgets/seeds; equal-completed-evaluation comparison; coverage ledger checkpoints showing the targeted cells; complete trial inventory including abandoned runs; explicit missing-api gaps recorded.
opportunities.next_action: Re-run .github/scripts/check_compatibility.py against your wheel, run the offline smoke to exercise the policy core, then preregister the comparison and freeze a compatible baseline before the first live run.

opportunities.title: Diversity-weighted batch composition using the public composer
opportunities.question: Does composing each batch with explicit diversity and parsimony pressure improve the yield rate at equal completed evaluator counts compared with fresh uniform batches?
opportunities.mechanism: The offline probe of openforage.search_templates.compose_next_batch established that a factory must return one mapping (batch entries are copies plus lineage='fresh_random'), a generator-returning factory yields an empty batch, prior entries must support .get, and non-graph payloads are dropped when max_depth is supplied. The full call contract remains unproved, so the composer is not used in any runnable path; the shipped challenger calls documented generator callables directly with max_depth=min(6, ctx.depth).
opportunities.primary_source_note: Cully and Demiris, Quality and Diversity Optimization: A Unifying Modular Framework. Starting point only; it does not prove the public composer improves outcomes.
opportunities.baseline_comparison: Baseline (installed genetic by default, random_weighted explicit) versus the composed-batch template under matched budgets and seeds, compared at equal completed evaluations with depth distribution from get_search_patterns as a secondary diagnostic. No full GA benchmark is claimed.
opportunities.acceptance_evidence: Composer call contract fully observed and recorded; depth-6 self-rejection proven by measure_graph_complexity; preregistered comparison; equal-count statistics; negative or inconclusive result recorded with the same rigor as a positive one.
opportunities.next_action: Keep using the stratified generator path; only wire the composer into a live run after proving the remaining contract with real graph objects, and record the limitation either way.

opportunities.title: Archive-guided novelty pressure on construction keys
opportunities.question: Does rewarding novelty of the construction key (rotation subfamily, feature family, depth) rather than the evaluator score widen valid coverage without lowering lifetime yield beyond the preregistered minimum effect?
opportunities.mechanism: Keep an archive of construction keys and de-prioritize candidates whose key is already dense in the archive, using only construction-time bookkeeping because per-candidate leaf introspection is not a public API. Novelty is keyed to what the generator controls, never inferred from private attributes.
opportunities.primary_source_note: Lehman and Stanley, Abandoning Objectives: Evolution Through the Search for Novelty Alone. Starting point, not superiority proof.
opportunities.baseline_comparison: Equal-count comparison against the campaign baseline (installed genetic by default; random_weighted explicit) with the preregistered minimum meaningful effect on lifetime_yield_rate and coverage breadth; exploratory label unless the full measured protocol holds and no full GA benchmark is claimed.
opportunities.acceptance_evidence: Archive size and key distribution recorded per checkpoint; depth cap proven; comparison at equal completed evaluations; usefulness metrics recorded with availability and provenance.
opportunities.next_action: Define the construction-key schema and preregister the novelty weight before sampling.

opportunities.title: Staged screening under equal evaluator budgets
opportunities.question: Can staged promotion of promising configurations reach the same qualifying-signal count with fewer completed evaluations than flat allocation?
opportunities.mechanism: Split each matched budget into preliminary and confirmation stages for template variants, promoting only variants that clear a preregistered early threshold. Resource limits cover simulations, wall-clock, CPU, RAM, storage, and concurrency only; no spend or token controls.
opportunities.primary_source_note: Li et al., A System for Massively Parallel Hyperparameter Tuning (ASHA asynchronous successive halving). The scheduling idea is the starting point; the public surface binds budgets to completed simulations, not server outcomes.
opportunities.baseline_comparison: Flat-budget baseline runs (installed genetic by default; random_weighted explicit) versus staged screening with total simulation budgets matched; compare at equal completed-evaluation totals and record wall-clock separately. No full GA benchmark is claimed.
opportunities.acceptance_evidence: Stage definitions and promotion thresholds preregistered; per-stage checkpoints; equal total budget accounting; abandoned variants retained in the trial inventory.
opportunities.next_action: Preregister stage sizes and the promotion metric; verify get_search_stats can segment the stages by era/config before running.

opportunities.title: Parsimony pressure at fixed depth cap
opportunities.question: Does preferring lower node-count graphs inside the depth-6 cap change lifetime yield or submission quality at equal completed evaluations?
opportunities.mechanism: Order candidates within a construction batch by complexity from measure_graph_complexity (node count) as a tie-breaker while holding depth <= 6, and compare against the same generator without the ordering. This tests complexity pressure independently of the depth cap.
opportunities.primary_source_note: MAP-Elites uses a parsimony-style tie-break in many implementations; cite it as the design ancestor, not as evidence for this specific effect.
opportunities.baseline_comparison: Same template with and without parsimony ordering, matched budgets and seeds, compared at equal completed evaluations; depth distribution reported as a control, with the installed genetic baseline default and random_weighted as the explicit alternative.
opportunities.acceptance_evidence: Complexity measurements recorded per candidate; depth cap proven; matched comparison; effect size and uncertainty or an explicit exploratory label.
opportunities.next_action: Confirm measure_graph_complexity returns node counts on yielded graph-like objects in your install before building the ordering.

opportunities.title: Surrogate-guided acquisition over construction parameters
opportunities.question: Can a cheap surrogate over construction parameters (rotation subfamily, feature family, depth) propose batches with a higher qualifying rate at equal completed evaluations?
opportunities.mechanism: Fit a surrogate on completed local evaluation outcomes and choose next construction parameters by an acquisition score. The observed public surface supports an explicit per-candidate simulate/result loop: openforage.simulate_signal(graph, *, named_universe=None, market_id, era_number, signal_pool_name, metaparameters=None, include_correlation=True, include_mi=True, record=True, return_series=False, return_weights=False, fail_fast=True) returns a SimulationHandle immediately, and the handle exposes status(), result() (block until completion, BacktestResult or raise), and cancel(). API presence (signatures/docstrings) is observed; live permissions, data availability, and behavior are untested, and the campaign must supply the real era/config/pool. Do not assume a successful simulation.
opportunities.primary_source_note: Snoek et al., Practical Bayesian Optimization of Machine Learning Algorithms. Starting point for acquisition design, not a measured claim here.
opportunities.baseline_comparison: Equal-count comparison against the campaign baseline (installed genetic by default; random_weighted explicit), with the acquisition fitted only on training-segment outcomes; blocked from any measured classification until simulate_signal permissions/data behavior are observed in a user-scoped campaign.
opportunities.acceptance_evidence: Requires per-candidate evaluator outcomes with timestamps from an observed simulate_signal/result loop, a user-supplied real era/config/pool, held-out segments, and preregistered acquisition parameters. Presence of the API alone is not evidence of live permissions, data access, or behavior.
opportunities.next_action: In a user-approved campaign with real scope/config, probe one bounded simulate_signal call and record status/result/cancel behavior and permissions; until then use only the delayed analytics surfaces, keep surrogate work exploratory, and never claim a successful simulation.
